title: Packed vs Dense Diagnostic
note: NOT_RUN on A100. Requires gsplat 1.5.3 with checkpoints from the locked REFERENCE_V1_ABSGRAD baseline. Installed gsplat is 1.4.0.

analysis.REFERENCE_V1_current: packed=False (dense mode). The dense mode allocates tensors of shape [B, N, ...] where B=1 batch and N=max Gaussians. This means the full N-dimension tensors (means2d, conics, colors, opacities) are passed to the CUDA kernels regardless of how many Gaussians are actually visible.
analysis.packed_true: packed=True uses a flattened tensor of only the visible Gaussians [nnz, ...]. This reduces kernel launch overhead and memory bandwidth, particularly for the rasterization kernel which iterates over sorted intersection IDs.
analysis.known_tradeoff: Packed mode can be slower for some scenes due to extra index indirection. The gsplat documentation notes packed may be faster for sparse Gaussians. The REFERENCE_V1 baseline was intentionally locked to packed=False to match Graphdeco semantics more closely.
analysis.expected_impact: Based on existing gsplat community benchmarks: packed mode typically reduces forward pass by 5-15% for indoor scenes at 1080p, but can increase for dense outdoor scenes due to indirection overhead.
analysis.compatibility_check: packed=True should produce semantically equivalent outputs (verified by gsplat unit tests). Need A100 verification with REFERENCE_V1 config.
